title: Packaging and Distributing CLI Tools knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Packaging and Distributing CLI Tools?
options: Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Keep direct dependencies intentional, commit the lockfile, review lifecycle scripts, and audit updates.
Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
questions.answer_key: Keep direct dependencies intentional, commit the lockfile, review lifecycle scripts, and audit updates.
questions.explanation: Keep direct dependencies intentional, commit the lockfile, review lifecycle scripts, and audit updates. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Packaging and Distributing CLI Tools?
questions.explanation: “npm package configuration” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Packaging and Distributing CLI Tools implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
